title: F1c: fork bug — string concat under --dce emits invalid core module
acceptance_criteria: Repro fails pre-patch, passes post-patch; compiler suite green; a concat-using example added to the green set.
notes:
Claimed by fork-fix subagent (F1c concat DCE bug); starting investigation in /home/rektide/src/zena-jco-fork.
Investigation started in /home/rektide/src/zena-jco-fork; will reproduce, fix compiler bootstrap DCE index desync, add compiler regression coverage, and verify build/suite.
Resolved in fork commits 691d8ed04dfb (failing regression) and cde81fc2a952 (fix). Root cause: packages/compiler/src/lib/analysis/usage.ts only marked ==/!= binary operator methods live; checker-resolved String.operator+ was omitted. Method-level DCE consequently left its ClassInfo MethodInfo at sentinel index -1, and packages/compiler/src/lib/codegen/expressions.ts encoded that signed LEB as 0x7f, interpreted by call as function index 127. This was not pending-helper/import index shifting. Fix follows resolvedOperatorMethod generically for binary and compound-assignment nodes, including overload-mangled names, while retaining != -> == handling. Regression compiles minimal String + and String += with dce:true, asserts WebAssembly.validate, instantiates, and returns length 2. Minimal + test: pre-fix 1 fail (validation false), post-fix 9/9 operator-DCE tests pass. Verification: npm run build green; npm test -w @zena-lang/compiler green (2313 tests, 2299 pass, 0 fail, 13 skipped, 1 todo).
close_reason: Fixed DCE reachability for resolved operator methods; minimal concat repro validates and executes, build and compiler suite are green.

title: F1d: fork — lazy/optional host stack-trace capture for component targets
description: Why: exception-using zena components (any try/catch) keep env.captureStackTrace/formatStackTrace (externref signatures, un-componentizable) even under --dce, because throw constructs Error whose new() calls the hook. Options: (a) target-conditional stdlib (error/host.zena vs error/component.zena with #stackTrace=null — mirrors the console swap seam), (b) lazy capture on first getStackTrace(), (c) jcona build absorbs the WAT rewrite. (a) is the clean fork fix; the E1-era reverted experiment chose exactly this shape before we knew it was load-bearing.

title: Host introspection LEAD: jco-side prototype (JS first)
description: Lead implementation for zenajco-host-introspection. Tier 1 (pure JS, no upstream): wrap shim resource objects + host-mediated imports to emit spans/events for every resource method call, lifetime, and WASI dispatch — extending the proven jcona-otel -I pattern; deliver interleaved guest+host traces. Tier 2 (stretch, upstream jco): expose the generated glue's handle->object tables (RESOURCE_SCOPE_* maps in js-component-bindgen output, currently module-private) — e.g. via the host-facing _util export; requires a js-component-bindgen (Rust) PR. Browser + Node legs.
acceptance_criteria: Tier 1: demo showing resource activity + host dispatch observable from JS in Node and browser. Tier 2 scoped: exact js-component-bindgen change identified (file:line) even if unsubmitted.
notes:
Claimed for lead implementation. Building jcona-observe Tier 1 imports instrumentation, guarded _util table-exposure transform wired into jcona transpile, and Node/browser observe-zena demo; will identify exact js-component-bindgen upstream seam and verify required green pipelines.
Completed lead implementation.

Tier 1: packages/jcona-observe exports observe(imports,{sink}), bounded JSON-safe value summaries (BigInt decimal, typed-array length + 16-byte preview, recursive arrays bounded), call-start/call-end/call-error events with interface/function/args/result/duration, resource-acquire/drop events, and observationSummary() counters per interface (calls, inFlight, resourceCalls, dropEvents). Returned resource instances are proxied while constructors stay untouched, preserving jco instanceof checks. Explicit drop/dispose/Symbol.dispose and flat [resource-drop] imports are observed; internal canonical drops that never cross the JS import boundary remain a Tier-2 concern. Generic EventSink<T> ({emit}) is shared with jcona-otel while legacy SpanSink {onSpan} remains supported.

Tier 2: jcona transpile --expose-resources calls a post-transpile transform pinned to @bytecodealliance/jco 1.33.0. It injects module._util.resourceTables.snapshot(). Shape: {shape,generatedFor,instances:[{id,resourceScopeId,resourceScopeTasks,asyncTasksByComponentIdx,asyncState,instanceFlags,handleTables,captureTables}]}. Map views are {size,entries}; handle tables decode live {handle,scope,rep,own} and free {handle,next} slots; capture values are summarized. Returned snapshots are deep-frozen copies, never raw mutable references. -I local tables register per-instantiation snapshot closures. Guard requires exactly one RESOURCE_SCOPE_ID, RESOURCE_SCOPE_TASKS, ASYNC_TASKS_BY_COMPONENT_IDX, ASYNC_STATE, INSTANCE_FLAGS, HANDLE_TABLES and _util plus the use-components directive; unknown/ambiguous shapes warn and remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

Upstream js-component-bindgen PR sketch (archive revision c03204df1c814253c5e88ae54ef6dbd80e961d0d): add opt-in read-only inspector at crates/js-component-bindgen/src/transpile_bindgen.rs:679-746 (write_util_export); register handleTableN/captureTableN where emitted at transpile_bindgen.rs:1427-1469; source state names from intrinsics/resource.rs:94-110, intrinsics/component.rs:89-126, intrinsics/p3/async_task.rs:306-363. In -I mode return inspector per instance through esm_bindgen.rs:202-287 / transpile_bindgen.rs:514-677 rather than retaining module-level registry; type it at ts_bindgen.rs:425-520. Observational snapshot only; mutation/forced drop is a separate ownership design. Full links and rationale: packages/jcona-observe/README.md.

Demo: examples/observe-zena runs -I async with one shared emit sink for guest spans + host events, and prints summary + table snapshot in Node and browser. Representative result: 4 spans, 31 host calls, 2 output-stream resource calls, 0 in-flight, 2 live own handles; resourceScopeId 32; captureTable1 has 2 summarized OutputStream values. Node: OBSERVE-ZENA-NODE-OK. Chrome: STATUS: OBSERVE-ZENA-BROWSER-OK: spans=4 hostCalls=31 resourceCalls=2 liveHandles=2 tableInstances=1.

Verification: jcona-observe 8/8 tests + tsgo + tsdown green; ./examples/otel-zena/run.sh green incl OTEL-ZENA-BROWSER-OK; ./examples/emoji-zena/run.sh green; final node examples/interop-matrix/run.mjs = 10 pass, 0 skip, 2 n/a, 0 fail.

Commits: 17df7f55 (observer, sink integration, guarded transform, CLI); f24f54eb (Node/browser demo, decoded handle/capture tables, docs/upstream sketch); 5fc9966d (recursive-summary hardening).

description: Why: operator wants zena code emitting spans. Guest-side lib/zena/otel emitting spans via WASI interfaces, host-side sink in the jcona pipeline (console first, OTLP later). Prereqs now exist: cabi strings + p2-direct externals. Blocked by W5 tooling for its verification pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A zena component emits spans observable from the host; documented interface choice (wasi:otel rc vs minimal custom); browser demo.
notes:
Sequenced behind zenajco-w5-tooling (epic, so no formal dep edge): verification pipeline should use the W5 tooling. GX queued.
starting: guest-authored telemetry via zena externals; researching wasi-otel WIT shapes vs custom world
Interface decision: option (a) — hand-written zena externals against the real wasi:otel/tracing@0.2.0-rc.2, NO custom jcona:otel world. A probe component (.test-agent/otel-probe, scratch) exercised every tracing function shape before the lib was written; no structural blocker found. Two preconceptions corrected by the probe: (1) wasi:otel tracing has no resources at all, so the wasi:io/streams method-handle precedent didn't transfer — what ships is flat params + hand-built record images; (2) indirect import results (current-span-context, wall-clock now) lower as a TRAILING RETURN-AREA PARAM (wasm-tools rejects [] -> [i32], wants [i32] -> []) — guest allocates, host writes, nested strings allocated through the guest's cabi_realloc export, guest frees. Lowerings: on-start = 9 flat i32 params; on-end = single ptr to a 168-byte span-data image (every field offset documented in lib/zena/otel/otel.zena and cross-checked against the jco transpile lifter, incl. list strides: key-value 16B, event 32B, link 36B).

Host wiring: jco transpile -I async + instantiate(undefined, imports) with unversioned key 'wasi:otel/tracing' → createTracing() from packages/jcona-otel, alongside preview2-shim namespaces (same pattern as interop-jshost compose.mjs). Sink pluggable (SpanSink interface gets full SpanData + depth + durationUs — OTLP-ready); default console sink, one line/closed span. Browsers import dist/tracing.mjs (tsdown) via import map.

Delivered: lib/zena/otel/otel.zena (startSpan/endSpan/endSpanError/setSpanAttr/withSpan + OtSpan handles); packages/jcona-otel (tracing host + console sink); examples/otel-zena (emoji pick inside emoji-demo > pick-emoji > draw-index/render-emoji spans, run.sh = thin jcona calls, host.mjs, index.html). Verified: run.sh exit 0 from clean state — Node prints the span tree with nesting/attrs/durations (e.g. 'span pick-emoji dur=3000µs emoji=😀') interleaved with guest stdout; jcona serve --check prints STATUS: OTEL-ZENA-BROWSER-OK with the same 4-span tree in headless Chrome. WIT vendored in examples/otel-zena/wit/deps.wit (wasi:otel clocks use repointed 0.2.0→0.2.12; metrics/logs omitted — tracing only).

Commits: 0df362c5 (lib), 84f01cb2 (host pkg), d6ed5bdb (example), f488a3ad (docs). v1 limits documented in the lib header (LIFO-vs-ancestors end order, ≤8 attrs/span, empty events/links, sign-cleared 127-bit ids, wall-clock µs granularity).
close_reason: Acceptance met: zena components emit observable spans through the real wasi:otel/tracing@0.2.0-rc.2 interface (hand-lowered externals — interface decision documented in notes + examples/otel-zena/README.md), with a pluggable-sink JS host (packages/jcona-otel), proven in BOTH Node (span tree printed by host sink interleaved with guest stdout) and browser (jcona serve --check → OTEL-ZENA-BROWSER-OK, headless Chrome). run.sh green from clean state (exit 0). Commits 0df362c5, 84f01cb2, d6ed5bdb, f488a3ad.
